Desirous

dih-ZY-ruhs · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Desirous is having or expressing a strong wish for something.

Desirous of privacy after the scandal, the family stopped answering their phone entirely.

Worked Example

Desirous of a life away from cameras, the retired actress bought a farmhouse under a different name.

The sentence names exactly what she wanted -- a private life -- and desirous simply signals that strong wish.

How Strong Is It? — interested → yearning → desirous

interested vs. desirous

interested vs. desirous: having curiosity or attention, without a strong wish

yearning vs. desirous

yearning vs. desirous: feeling an intense, often wistful, longing

Build the Word

The pieces

root — desire

root — desire: a strong wish or longing for something (Latin desiderare)

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: possessing the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Desirous is simply desire ('a strong wish for something') plus -ous, 'full of.' Someone desirous of something is, quite literally, full of desire for it.

Use the root in a new word: desire

Use the root in a new word: desire: His only desire after the long expedition was a hot shower and a full night's sleep.

Word Choice

Desirous is fairly formal -- in conversation, most people would just say 'eager for' or 'hoping for' instead.
